title: Hookable Terraform modules and overlay shims for customer VPC customizations
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Design and implement a set of 'hookable' Terraform modules and lightweight overlay shims to enable customer-specific VPC customizations without forking core modules. Goal is to make per-customer variations (route tables, transit gateways, custom subnets, security posture exceptions) composable, testable, and safe to upgrade across Redwood Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Core modules expose stable, minimal interfaces and documented hook points (input objects, locals, child_module call hooks).
2) Overlay shims live in a customer overlays registry (git submodule or mono-repo path) and can be composed via a small "composer" pattern without modifying core TF.
3) Upgrades to core modules do not require manual edits to overlays for >90% of customers; when a breaking change occurs, an "upgrade shim" pattern provides automated migration steps and plan-time warnings.
4) Health-check outputs (HTTP endpoint, Prometheus metrics labels) are configurable by overlays and exported to the console's onboarding telemetry.
5) CI runs terratest/plan-diff and an automated canary apply for a representative set of overlay combinations before tagging release.
6) Conformance tests added for drift detection and rollback safety in the infra pipeline.
implementation_notes:
Design patterns: 
- Hookable module interface: prefer object inputs (map/object) with documented keys and a 'hooks' block that accepts lists of 'pre' and 'post' snippets (implemented as child modules or module compositions) so overlays can inject resources without touching core logic.
- Overlay shims: small Terraform modules that either: (a) override variables via an overlay composer (patch-style HCL that merges with defaults at plan time), or (b) provide optional child modules referenced by core through conditional module blocks.
- Versioning: add a module_version input and a lightweight compatibility metadata file (module_compat.yaml) in core modules. The composer validates overlay compatibility during CI.
- Upgrade shims: for breaking changes, provide a migration module (shim) that can be applied in the same workspace to perform safe resource replacement patterns (create new resource, move references via outputs, destroy old once traffic is drained). Documented runbook for manual intervention.
- Health checks: core networking modules export a resource "redwood_network_health_check" with outputs: health_url, prometheus_labels, last_checked_timestamp. Overlay modules can opt into registering additional checks by calling an exported 'health_register' child module.
- Testing: add terratest suites that instantiate core + overlay permutations (minimal, transit-gateway, custom-routes) and assert plan-diff size thresholds and stable state after module upgrades. Integrate plan-diff gating and an approval workflow for changes that exceed thresholds.
- Composer tooling: small CLI (iac-compose) to merge overlay variables and produce a flattened tfvars for CI; supports dry-run and a 'compat-check' mode to fail fast if overlay touches removed variables.
- Rollout strategy: blue/green or canary applies for customer workspaces via the infra pipeline; automatic rollback on health-check regressions.
Operational notes: support team will run a one-time compare for customers with heavy customizations and propose migration shims. Provide examples and templates in the repo under examples/overlays/.
